title: Exercise 7A · Q9(e)
summary: Find AD in ΔABD, then DC = AC − AD, then BC in ΔCBD.
alt: Exercise 7A · Q9(e): In the figure, BD ⊥ AC, BD = 32 cm, AB = 40 cm and AC = 55 cm. Find the value of e, the length of BC.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: In the figure, **BD ⊥ AC**. **BD = 32 cm**, **AB = 40 cm** and **AC = 55 cm**. We have to find **e**, the length of **BC**.

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔABD, **∠D = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **AB**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides. We want a shorter side, so subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AB^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{AD^2} \\ \role{legB}{AD^2} &= \role{hyp}{AB^2} - \role{legA}{BD^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and subtract
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AB^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{AD^2} \\ \role{legB}{AD^2} &= \role{hyp}{AB^2} - \role{legA}{BD^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{40^2} - \role{legA}{32^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1600} - \role{legA}{1024} \\ &= \role{legB}{576}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: Take the square root of both sides (a length is positive).\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AB^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{AD^2} \\ \role{legB}{AD^2} &= \role{hyp}{AB^2} - \role{legA}{BD^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{40^2} - \role{legA}{32^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1600} - \role{legA}{1024} \\ &= \role{legB}{576} \\ \role{legB}{AD} &= \sqrt{576} = 24\ \text{cm}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Find DC
steps.narration: **DC** is what is left of **AC** after taking away **AD**.\[\begin{aligned}DC &= AC - AD \\ &= 55 - 24 = 31\ \text{cm}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔCBD, **∠D = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **BC**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{BC^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{DC^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and add
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and add.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{BC^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{DC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{32^2} + \role{legB}{31^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{1024} + \role{legB}{961} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1985}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 1985 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{BC^2} &= \role{legA}{BD^2} + \role{legB}{DC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{32^2} + \role{legB}{31^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{1024} + \role{legB}{961} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1985} \\ \role{hyp}{BC} &= \sqrt{1985} = \role{ans}{44.6\ \text{cm}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Check DC
challenges.prompt: AC = 55 cm and AD = 24 cm. How long is **DC**?

takeaways: Pythagoras' theorem works only in **right-angled** triangles — mark every right angle in the figure first.
Split the figure into right-angled triangles and solve them **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next triangle.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
